lines.en: I knock on Touka’s door and don’t have anything creative to say about it.
So I decide to knock a second time just to make things slightly more interesting.
: Come in?
I save my third knock for when my creativity fully dies and Touka will no longer let me into her room.
At this rate, something like that could happen any day.
Because, while the two of us can have serious conversations on occasion (Normally while I’m interrupting her morning practices), she’s still Touka at the end of the day.
She’s not on the same level as everyone else and, even if she does like (or tolerate) me now, that could change at any given moment.
Her family will always come first because that’s just...the type of family she’s from.
And no matter what I do (or want to do) to her, nothing will change that.
Probably.
: I believe this is the part where I’m supposed to act surprised by your arrival, but your impatience reared its head at the door and I was able to realize it was you a bit earlier than normal today.
: Good day to you as well, madam.
: Why are you all dressed up? It’s been a while since I’ve seen you in that outfit.
: I abstain from wearing it around the city as I’ve come to realize it’s a bit too lavish to be perceived as “normal.” Plus, dressing in commoner-attire prevents me from being attacked.
: This dress is worth more than your home and I’d prefer it remains both on my body and out of the wrong person’s hands.
: So what I’m hearing is the “right” person would be able to get their hands on said body so long as you remain clothed.
: Of course that’s what you’re hearing. You are a pervert. And to that I say- please back away. I am carrying mace.
: Will do. But you still haven’t told me what the occasion is.
: I must not have received the memo advising me that I must inform you of my every action. Please forgive me.
: It’s okay, you’re forgiven. What’s going on?
: Do I need to send a second memo?
: I’m on my way to the manor to take care of some business with my mother. And I intended to go there alone, but I now feel pressured to invite you on account of how “clingy” you are tonight.
: I’m not clingy. I just miss you and appreciate all you do for both the class and me.
: You absolutely do not. But I will allow you to come regardless. I do ask that you remain on your best behavior, though. From what I understand, this is going to be a serious meeting.
: Serious? You don’t think it’s about the apartment complex, do you?
: I do not. Because, and brace yourself for this, Sensei- the world does not revolve around you. The Tsukioka Foundation has much more to worry about than some trivial side project I took up.
: The world doesn’t revolve around your family either. Which is why you should all surrender your wealth to me and let me take up the mantle as the new Tsukioka figurehead.
: If you’re going to propose, at least do it in a proper, less self-absorbed way. Of course I won’t say yes to that.
: You’re sure it’s cool if I come with you? I don’t want to interrupt whatever “important business” you have going on. Especially now that I know it’s business that doesn’t directly pertain to me.
: I’m sure it will be fine. The worst case scenario is that you’ll be forced to wait out the night in a private room while I take care of whatever it is that needs to be done.
: But it would be less like “solitary confinement” and more like being sequestered in a three-star Holiday Inn Express.
This message has been brought to you in part by Holiday Inn Express.
At Holiday Inn Express hotels, we keep it simple...and smart.
Book your stay today.
: That doesn’t sound so bad. I’ve always wanted to stay in a Holiday Inn Express.
: Why?
: Because they keep it simple and smart.
: Oh. Well, okay. I suppose this works out quite well then.
: We mustn’t delay any further, though. My limousine is already waiting outside.
: If you’d please follow me, Sensei...
Touka reaches out her hand to guide me but, when I attempt to grab it, she takes it back and makes me look like an idiot.
I have no idea who taught her this, but my newest goal in life is to find them and eliminate them.
Or, if it is someone I am actively having sex with (Which is very possible from a sheer mathematic point of view), to eliminate them in a different way.
With my penis.
What I mean is that I’m going to have really violent sex with them.
But anyway, Touka and I hop into the limo and, after a smooth and quiet ride over to the manor, we begin to make our way through an area that is becoming rather familiar to me.
How that happened is still a little strange but, then again, what isn’t nowadays?

If you told me two years ago that I’d one day be memorizing the layout of a rich girl’s mansion, I probably would have assumed your name was Ayane and then asked you to stop speaking with my dick in your mouth.

But that’s not the case at all. In fact, my dick rarely finds its way into Ayane’s mouth at all anymore because we’re either too busy having real sex like human beings or learning things about the end of the world.
I wonder for a moment how long it will be before Touka makes it to that point.
Not the sex part — the latter. But of course, I wholeheartedly welcome the idea of having sex with her prior to that.
And with the way she smiles at me sometimes, I feel as if that’s not all that far away.
I know it’s just politeness, though.
I know this is how she was raised.
I know there must have been countless men and women before me who were shown this same exact smile in this same exact dress.
And I know it always went nowhere.
But that doesn’t stop me from wanting to be an outlier.
And it can not quell the incessant fantasies of tearing that dress off of her.
: You’re thinking something inappropriate, aren’t you?
: Me? Never.
: Perhaps I should just sequester you now and save myself the mace?
: Yeah...that would probably be best for everyone.
: You really are like a child sometimes, Sensei.
: Meanwhile, I have a hard time believing you ever acted like a child. At least not in this setting. The real world is another story entirely.
: I’m getting there. But you’re not far off in your assumption of how I was at home.
: For as long as I can remember, I’ve been showered with praise. For my behavior...My talent...My understanding of the role that I was born into.
: But of course, such praise was not simply gifted to me. Everything I was and everything I am was earned.
: I lost count of how many different lessons I’ve taken over the years. And for things that won’t even matter, no less.
: How to hold a fork. How to play piano. The names of different types of forks. French. The position forks need to be placed in.
: There were so many lessons about forks! Why?!
: Being rich sounds weird.
: It is so incredibly strange at times. Especially in hindsight. And I sometimes find myself envying my sister as her schedule is significantly less packed than mine was at her age.
: But again, this was the role that I was born into. And as the eldest daughter of Tomonori and Tsubasa Tsukioka, there are certain things expected of me.
: I suppose you could even say I lack the freedom to discover who I am on my own as it was already predetermined the moment I entered this world.
: And yet...I do not hate it.
: You don’t?
: I don’t.
: Perhaps it’s due to my future being figuratively beaten into me since I was young, but I never fancied or even...I suppose comprehended any other sort of life.
: Without any idea of what I could want, I was left to only want one thing. And that thing is plastered to a slowly rising sun that will one day shine for me and no one else.
: As if it doesn’t shine for you already.
: I understand why you’d say that. To you and many others, it must seem that I already have everything I could ever want.
: But what can not be seen is my want for wanting something.
: What can not be seen is the cage that keeps me from taking flight.
: The most depressing part is that the door of that cage has been open this entire time. And I’ve been perfectly capable of leaving it.
: But among a ruthless regime of fork-based lessons and lectures on etiquette, I was also taught that I wanted to stay inside of that cage...so there was never a reason to leave at all.
: And now, it’s so ingrained into the way I think that it’s as if I’ve inherited every last bit of my mother. And my father. And those who lived before me.
: Decades and decades of customs and expectations and rules flow through my blood like crocodiles in the Nile.
: They’re simply a part of me now. They can not be removed, nor do I want them to be. But I know their existence was not of my own choosing, which makes it all feel a bit false at times.
: Nothing against crocodiles, of course. I’m sure they love their home just as much as I do.
: Isn’t it...boring, though? Already knowing your future?
: It can be.
: But my life is not entirely devoid of excitement now that you and the others have nestled into it.
Touka stops walking and I don’t notice right away.
But when I turn around, she isn’t gazing up at the moon or...wistfully watching the stars and correlating them to some grand idea of how expansive the universe is.
She’s looking at me.
She’s looking at something that stood beneath her cage and shouted catcalls at her until she was forced to leave it.
And it wasn’t until she was outside that she realized just how expansive that universe really is.
It wasn’t the stars at all.
It was all of us.
: What? Why are you looking at me like that?
: Like what?
: Like that. Like you’re-
: My mother?
: Ahh...you really have been spending more time with her lately, haven’t you?
: Should I be worried?
: What would you have to worry about?
: That you’ll see just how...unoriginal I am.
: I mean...don’t get me wrong. You two clearly have a lot in common. But there’s plenty I’ve seen in you that I’ve yet to see in her.
: I’m assuming those sample sizes are rather skewed in my favor, though. And I wonder if you’ll say the same when you come to know her just as well.
: I doubt Tsubasa is the type to let anyone know her that well.
: And I am?
: So far. You might also be capable of sly, behind-the-scenes manipulation- but you’ll need way more practice if you’re ever going to get to her level.
: You know her better than I thought.
: Her intentions are good, though. And I trust her judgement entirely.
: It does seem that way most of the time. The way she goes about things just makes me feel a little weird. Like I’m the sidekick to the world’s most lawfully good vigilante or something.
: Hmm...I’m not sure if you’re fit to be her “sidekick” just yet.
: But I wouldn’t mind you being mine.
: Oh yeah? And what would my duties include? Making sure you don’t have any sort of original thought? Filtering all your opinions through your mother and trying to get them approved?
: Ha ha ha. Clever. But I’ll have you know that sharing the same values and ideals as her does not make me a complete clone. I’m still Touka Tsukioka when all is said and done.
: Until your corporate robo-family asks you to be something else.
: They will not ask. They will expect. And I will likely do as they want as that is how I was grown.
: With the one exception being an arranged marriage?
: I...beg your pardon?
: Your mom told me a while ago that they had several “suitors” picked out for you, but that you never seemed comfortable with the idea.
: Why on earth would she tell you that? How did that topic even come up?
: No clue. But if you’re so dead set on playing the role, why was that an issue?
: Hah...
: It wasn’t.
: What do you mean?
: I mean that I would have followed through with it if it needed to be done.

: As the family’s heir, it is my responsibility that we maintain our status once my parents pass away. And if joining families with another influential house would secure such a status, I would comply.
: Then why-
: Because you do not always have to be “comfortable” with something to know that it must be done. That is especially true for people in power.
: If my family had always taken the “comfortable” path, we’d be nowhere near where we are today.
: So...what? You’d just let some random guy from another family knock you up for status?
: Would you rather it be you?
: That...wait. No. That’s not what I was-
: As much as I appreciate my mother’s kindness and consideration, I would do whatever I believed to be best for my family.
: But...thankfully...I don’t have to.
: You see, there’s no one here who could elevate our family any further. At least not with the city closed-off. So I’m free to marry someone I love instead.
: I just wonder if I can ever find it in myself to do that.
: To be completely honest, I’m not sure I’d make a very good wife in the first place. A mother, perhaps. But I’m not sure if I could tolerate someone like you pestering me all day, every day.
: It sounds fun, though. Right?
: Fun? Please. That sounds like the single most exhausting thing I’ve ever heard of.
: And that’s not even counting what we’d get up to at night.
: Are you sure I’m not a bit too womanly for your tastes? What, with you fancying girls of Maya’s stature and all.
: That was...not a thing you were supposed to see.
: But I did. And now I know, so ha.
: Touka...
: Sensei, if you’re that desperate to marry into the family, perhaps Tsukasa would be more in line with your...tastes?
: Tsukasa? Just what kind of person do you think I am?
: Someone who should not be allowed within five miles of a school.
: Touka, I am not going to marry Tsukasa. And I really wish you and your mom would stop trying to-
: Peasant!
